thread.title: The Nintendo GameCube's Hidden Gems

author: screenrant
title: The Nintendo GameCube's Hidden Gems
text:
The Nintendo GameCube may not have received as many games as the PlayStation 2, but its hit rate was notably high. The console delivered a few great first-party Nintendo exclusives, as well as some perfect experiences from other developers. The GameCube had a number of standout titles that showcase its unique charm and innovative gameplay.
The Nintendo GameCube may not have received as many games as the PlayStation 2, but its hit rate was notably high. The console delivered a few great first-party Nintendo exclusives, as well as some perfect experiences from other developers.
One of the standout titles is Tales of Symphonia, an RPG that simply does everything right. At a glance, Tales of Symphonia looks like any other cartoony, charming entry in the Tales franchise, but looks can be deceiving. While the game doesn't innovate to the same degree as some other genre titans, it delivers across the board without ever missing a beat.
With a likable cast of characters, a story that never stops developing, and a world packed with interesting characters to meet and secrets to discover, Tales of Symphonia avoids ever falling into the slog of repetition that can drag down even the best JRPGs. An action-based combat system further contributes to its engaging pace, and a balanced difficulty that skews slightly easy means you won't get bogged down in many frustrating boss fights.
Metroid Prime is another example of Nintendo's proficiency at bringing 2D franchises to the third dimension. Like Super Mario 64 and Ocarina of Time, Super Metroid turned the Metroid series into an immediate 3D powerhouse without losing the appeal of its 2D predecessors. Metroid Prime is a first-person shooter, but it's still much more of an adventure game that happens to involve shooting from a first-person perspective.
The biggest joys lie in traversing the game's atmospheric environments and uncovering power-ups necessary for progress. Pikmin is the kind of game that shouldn't be perfect, but somehow it is. The unique take on the real-time strategy genre is unlike anything that came before it, and it would be only reasonable for Nintendo to make a few missteps along the way.
However, the first adventure of Captain Olimar is as impeccable as it is innovative. Pikmin tasks the player with open-ended environmental puzzles that can only be solved through the use of Pikmin, which feature a suite of different abilities according to their color. The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker was first revealed to be the farthest thing from a perfect Zelda game that plenty of fans could imagine.
However, when it launched, critics sang its praises, and its reputation has only grown over the years. The game's cute, cartoon aesthetic may have been a departure from its predecessors, but it delivered something unique and charming. The game's story and characters are well-developed, and the game's pacing is well-balanced. Overall, the GameCube had a number of standout titles that showcase its unique charm and innovative gameplay
